sourceFull: Data: Deccan Herald (Jul 2025); World Bank, What a Waste 2.0

parts: Every day, Bengaluru throws away more than six thousand tonnes of waste.
That's heavier than a thousand elephants. Every single day.
And too much of it ends up where we walk:
on footpaths, in corners, in empty plots.
It's homes, collectors, trucks, sorting centres and recyclers, each working alone, each blind to the others.
And this isn't just Bengaluru. The world throws away about two billion tonnes a year,
and that could reach three point four billion by twenty fifty.
What if every link in the chain could see the whole chain?
Pickups planned around what each street actually needs.
Every load tracked, from doorstep to recycler.
Collectors paid fairly, and on time.
A.L.K.I. is being designed to plan systems like this.
OmniChain, to keep a record no one can quietly edit.
And OmniBot is being built for the dirty, dangerous work no one should have to do.
It takes residents, workers, recyclers, and the people who run our cities, working from the same truth.
In nature, there is no waste. Everything returns to the cycle.
Six thousand tonnes a day. Let's turn it back into a cycle.
